_what: Lists as data (src/lists.mjs): the kinds of field a list can have (each with the icon its values and its column lead with), the limits every list keeps, and the words its refusals use. A new kind of field is one row here; the lists module never names a kind. A kind that says `reads_outside` works its values out from records outside the lists (progress from work references, a relationship from messages), so a read of a list holding one depends on more than the lists and is read again on every change (src/lists.mjs dependsOf).

open_rows._why: A list whose field names an open_index keeps its rows not settled in that declared index (src/record-indexes.json), so reading what is open never loads the settled rows, which only grow. A row put with that field unset starts at the field's `starts` value, so the index misses none; rows written before that gain it fill_page rows at a time, and the progress is the record <mark_type>:<list>.

field_kinds.label: Long text
field_kinds._what: Written and read as a document (markdown): the first such field is each row's notes, edited with the documents editor wherever a row is opened.

field_kinds.label: Name from records
field_kinds._what: A name chosen with the shared record picker. The field declares from (lists, row_types and/or holds), and optionally new (where an explicitly requested missing row is made). Lists keep the chosen title as text, so existing name values and title-based filters still work; this is a name, not an identity link (use link for that). The picker transport JSON is decoded before storage, never displayed or compared as JSON.

carries._what: A value worked out from the row's other values by the formula engine: derive.request.binding is the formula (a formula-engine binding, e.g. { "$kind": "binding", "select": { "from": "self", "path": ["minutes"] }, "transform": [{ "op": "op:core.mul", "args": { "value": 60 } }] }); inside a transform step's args, a nested binding's `self` is the value so far, so it reads another field of the same row with `from: "context"` (e.g. { "op": "op:core.div", "args": { "value": { "$kind": "binding", "select": { "from": "context", "path": ["channel_median"] } } } }; end with { "op": "op:core.to_number" } to get a number rather than exact decimal text); context_from_fields names the fields it reads (every kept field when left out).

Read-only bounded progress. Set source_field to a row field holding a work reference, or done_field and total_field to numeric fields plus evidence_field. tree_field may name a row field containing a JSON job tree; only verified completed leaves count, and it is used when source_field cannot be measured. Unknown scope or missing evidence reads as Not measured.

field_kinds.label: Picture, video or file
field_kinds._what: One of the person's files, by its identity (1f:...) or its name (/Media/clip.mp4). Lists and pages show it as the picture, video or sound it is; a shared or published copy of the list serves its bytes through that same link.

field_kinds.label: Shown when
field_kinds._what: A rule over the row's own values and the moment it is read (now, a date in milliseconds; opened, how many times the link showing it was opened): the formula engine's tree { kind: "group", combinator, negate, rules: [{ kind: "rule", field, operator, params }] }. In a shared or published copy of the list the row shows only while its rule holds, so a row can start, stop, come back, or appear after so many views; the list itself shows every row.

field_kinds.label: Applies when
field_kinds._what: A rule over the facts a place is chosen by (src/place-lists.mjs: what is known about a list to keep, or a piece of work to run): the formula engine's tree { kind: "group", combinator, negate, rules: [{ kind: "rule", field, operator, params }] } over the facts its kind declares (src/place-lists.json). A row of a places list is chosen only while its rule holds; a row without one always may be. It never leaves in a shared copy.

field_kinds.label: Done once
field_kinds._what: A rule over what one of the person's devices reports about itself (src/device-facts.mjs: a page on a Mac says which cameras it sees as `cameras`, the iPhone app says whether a switch is on as `<switch>.on`): the formula engine's tree { kind: "group", combinator, negate, rules: [{ kind: "rule", field, operator, params }] } with each fact as a text field. On the person's Waiting on you list a row whose rule passes on one device's facts is marked Done by itself. It never leaves in a shared copy.

field_kinds.label: Done when (Trillion checks)
field_kinds._what: What done means, as a check Trillion makes itself against what is true now (src/done-when.mjs, src/done-when-facts.json): { over, match, tree, says }. `over` is a facts source id (saved-logins, connections, computer-sources, device-facts, files, arrived, work, or list:<list id>; arrived is what one of the person's own places brought, such as a route of Downloads with text containing .cer for a certificate download); `tree` is the formula engine's rule group { kind: "group", combinator, negate, rules: [{ kind: "rule", field, operator, params }] } over that source's rows (their fields are in src/done-when-facts.json); `match` says how many of the source's rows must pass the tree: all, any (at least one) or none; `says` is the plain words of what is counted, read after "<passing> of <all> " (for example "logins your AIs can read"). On the person's Waiting on you list a row whose check passes is set Done by itself when what waits is read and whenever a source changes, and its card says how far it is. It never leaves in a shared copy.

carries._what: A value worked out on every read from the rows a link field of the same row names (src/list-rollups.mjs): rollup.through is that link field (left out, the row itself is the one row reached), rollup.field a field of the list it links to (a rollup or formula of that list too: its computed value is read, never following a link back to a row being worked out), rollup.where an optional rule tree, the kind a saved view keeps, that a reached row must pass to count (a value written { "settles_of": "<field id>" } is the values that field of the linked list settles on), rollup.op a row of `aggregates` (count, sum, average, min, max, distinct, values for the linked values themselves ...), run by the formula engine. Nothing is kept in the row, so it is never out of date.

Always derived, never typed: worked out on every read from the records that name this row (messages mentioning them, arrivals they spoke in; src/list-relationships.json sources), through the store's participation index (src/list-relationships.mjs). relationship.attribute is a row of src/list-relationships.json attributes: first_interaction, last_interaction, next_interaction, last_message, last_heard, interactions or strength.

A value worked out on every read from the values another field of the same row has held (src/list-value-history.mjs): history.field names a field that says keeps_history: true, history.op a row of value_history.ops (value_at with at or days_ago, previous_value, value_set_at, time_spent_in with value and unit, has_been_in with value). It answers null when the history it needs is not kept.

A button on every row that runs a Workshop tool: action.definition_ids names the tool, action.label the button's words, action.input fixed inputs, and action.copy maps the row's values to the tool's inputs ({ key: <tool input>, from: "answers.<field id>" } or "record.title"). The tool receives only the inputs its own schema takes.

naming._what: A field that names a thing is a link to it (src/naming-fields.mjs). A text, choice or tags field whose distinct values are, at least match_share of them and at least least_values, each the title of exactly one row of one other list names that list's rows; a field named in named_by_field names the rows of the list given there (made once when missing). Either way the field becomes a link to that list and each value its row id, a row made, titled by the value, where none has it. A field that says what it names (`names: { list }`, set by the person or their AI) is moved whatever its words are, and a row it makes fills its own link fields with the rows of their lists its words name (titles of at least least_title_chars, as whole words; never the one row the words came from). A field a saved view, a public page, a start or a settle reads by its words, the title field, and a value longer than value_chars are never moved. Lists marked by a change are looked at again at idle (mark_type), one field moved per step, a look over every list starting at most once every every_minutes.
naming._named_by_field: Fields that name a kind of thing by their id, with the list that keeps it: { fields: [ids], list: { id, label, row_type, title_field, fields } }. Empty until a person's own words show such a field holds names: on 2026-10-10 the CRM's company field held how a person is known ("Dad", "UAB Theta Chi", "Tennis Student"), not companies, so moving it would make a list of companies named Dad.

holds._what: What a list holds, by what it is made of rather than what it is called (src/lists.mjs search `holds`, holders). A list holds `people` when its row type is one of row_types or any of its fields has a kind in field_kinds, so a CRM the person built under any name is found by what is in it (a name with an email or a phone), not by a row type this file would have to guess.

aggregates._what: What read_list_aggregates can work out over a list or one of its saved views without sending the rows: each row here is a measure. `rows` measures count the rows themselves; the others take a field's values (`kinds`: the rule kinds of the fields it applies to, empty for any) and run `transform` over them as the formula engine's array operators (src/list-aggregates.mjs gives the engine the values as `values`). A new measure is one row here; nothing in the code names one.

q._what: The share of the values that lie at or below the answer, 0 to 1: 0.5 is the median, 0.9 the value 9 in 10 are under, 0 the smallest, 1 the largest. Between two values it interpolates (the way a spreadsheet's PERCENTILE does).

latest.label: Latest

by._what: The field whose value says which row is latest (a date, a number or text that sorts), the largest wins and the later row wins a tie. Without it the row that comes last in the read is the latest.

latest._what: The current value: the field's value on the most recent row that holds one, of any kind of value (a mood, a status, a reading).

weighted.label: Weighted count

weights._what: A weight for each value of the field ({ "goal": 3, "assist": 2 }); every row adds the weight of its value.

default._what: The weight of a value the map does not name.

weighted._what: A count where each row counts as its value's weight, not as 1.

streak.label: Streak

period._what: The calendar period a streak is counted in (UTC; a week starts on Monday).

times._what: How many different days of a period must hold a row for the period to count.

now._what: The moment the streak is counted back from (an ISO time); the time of the read when absent.

streak._what: Consecutive periods, counting back from the one holding now, in each of which `times` different days have a row. A period in progress that has not yet met the target does not break the streak; the one before it anchors it.

values.label: The linked values
values._what: A lookup: the values themselves, each once. per_row: only a rollup field reads it (over one row's linked rows), never a total over a whole list.

pairs._what: Two link fields that are one relationship seen from both sides (src/list-pairs.mjs): a field names the field on the list it links to that holds the way back (`pairs_with`), and both are link fields pointing at each other's list. A write to either side changes the other in the same write: a row added to one side is added to the other, a row taken away (or removed) is taken from it. Each side keeps its own max_links, so one-to-many and many-to-many are what the two sides say, never stored. Saving a field that pairs with one that names nothing yet names it back in the same write; two fields whose pointers do not mirror each other are refused.

keys._what: Identity keys (src/list-keys.mjs). A field marked `unique` holds a value no other row of the list holds in its shared form (src/list-identity.mjs normalizers): a second row with the same email, domain or phone is refused naming the row that has it. Each held form is a record of its own, <type>:<list>:<field>:<BLAKE3 of the form>, naming the row, written in the same write as the row, so asking whether a form is taken is one point read whatever the list's size. Rows kept before a field was unique gain theirs open_rows.fill_page at a time (the progress is <open_rows.mark_type>:<mark><list>); until that is done a write that sets a unique field is refused as being prepared, never guessed. `match_modes` are what put_list_rows match_mode may say: what a row matched by match_on may do.

stamps._what: Who wrote each value (src/list-stamps.mjs), for a list that says `stamps: true` (none does unless asked). Every field a write sets carries { class, by, at } in the row's _stamps; a cleared field loses it. The class comes from the writer's name (actor.by, lowercased) by the first row of `classes` whose pattern it matches, else `default`. A value whose class is in `machine` reads as machine-written (`machine_written` on the row), so a person can see what a person typed and what was worked out for them. A field that says `machine: true` always reads as machine-written when it holds a value.

history._what: What a removed row leaves (src/lists.mjs putRows, removedRows, restoreRows). A removal writes a trash record <trash_type>:<list>:<row> { list_id, row_id, removed_at, by } beside it, so the list's recently removed rows are read newest first from the declared index (src/record-indexes.json) and a row is put back from the log, exactly as it was before its removal (restore_list_rows). A trash record older than trash_days is no longer listed, and a removal lets go of this list's oldest expired ones (limits.trash_purged_per_write at a time). A merge leaves a tombstone <tombstone_type>:<list>:<row> { merged_into }, so a read of the old id answers where it went and a link written later to the old id is written to the row it became (followed at most limits.tombstone_hops times).

review._what: Keeping what a list says true (src/list-review.mjs): a list set up for review has an owner, a review state and a date by which it must be checked again on each row (`fields`, by role), and saved views that decide, with the formula engine's rules, which rows need review and why (`views`; a field names a role, `title` is the list's title field). `actions` are what review_list_rows may do to rows: set a state, set the date a review lasts for (expires_days, the list's own or this default), clear it, name who checked or who owns. read_rows_needing_review reads the views and answers each owner the rows they must look at, with the reasons.

proposals._what: Changes an AI proposes to a list and a person approves (src/list-proposals.mjs). A proposal names the rows it may change (`editable`, at most editable_most, each checked against the caller's right to write the list), the places it looked for its evidence (`scopes`, at most scopes_most: a list, or a saved view of one; with none it cites nothing) and the evidence itself (rows within those scopes), and holds the rows' new values beside what they held when it was made (`saw`). Nothing changes until a person decides: approve applies it exactly once, all or nothing, refusing it as conflicted when a row it changes was changed since; decline, withdraw (its proposer) and remove close it. A list that says review_changes: true refuses direct writes from a writer the `gated` rows name (an AI over MCP), pointing it at propose_list_changes; a list that does not say it stays open to every writer.

use_heat._what: How much a row is used, decaying with time (src/list-review.mjs): use_list_rows adds `add` to a row's heat, which halves every half_life_days; one use keeps a row warm for one half-life (cold_below is half of add); a row is touched at most once every min_gap_minutes (a second use in that time is not written), so heat costs at most one small record per row per gap. read_cold_list_rows lists rows whose heat is below cold_below, a page at a time within scan_rows, leaving out rows whose review is current (a person said they are true).

value_history._what: A field that says keeps_history: true keeps on its row the values it has held, each with when it began and who wrote it (src/list-value-history.mjs `_history`: { cut, steps: [{ v, at, by, via }] }), written with the value. A `history` field reads them through one of `ops`: `reduce` is the interval arithmetic (at: the value held at a moment; previous: the value before the current one; since: when the current one began; duration: time spent holding a value, in `unit`; ever: whether it was ever held), `needs` what the field must say, `answers` the kind a view compares (source: the kind of the field it reads). A field keeps at most steps_kept steps; older ones are let go and the field says cut, so an answer that needs them is null.

view_records._what: A saved view kept as a record of its own (src/lists.mjs saveView), <type>:<list>:<view> { list_id, view, order }, so adding, ordering, sharing or removing one view never rewrites the list or its other views. order is a fractional key; the declared index (src/record-indexes.json) reads a list's views in order. Views a list kept inside itself before are read as before, ahead of its own; moving a view gives every view of the list a record of its own first.

store_narrows._what: The filter rules the records door decides itself (records:list `where`: each named top-level field equal, as JSON, to one value), so a list page reads only the rows such a rule keeps instead of every row (src/workspace/list-records.ts whereOf). Each row is an operator of parts/formula-engine/rules/rule-operators.json and how its rule names the one value: `param` the rule's param holding a list of exactly one value, or `equals` the value itself. A rule in force that is not here (case-blind text, words, ranges, negations, an `or` of several) is decided over every row the page reads.

filters._what: A saved filter kept as a resource of its own (src/list-filters.mjs), <type>:<list>:<filter> { list_id, filter: { id, label, rules } }, apart from any view. A view or another filter uses it by putting { kind: "filter", filter_id } where a rule goes in a rule group; reading the view puts the filter's group there, so one change to a filter changes every view that uses it. A filter may use others down to limits.filter_depth levels; a filter that reaches itself is refused.

snapshots._what: A view's rows held still (src/list-snapshots.mjs): a snapshot is the ids a list or saved view held when it was taken, kept as <type>:<id>, read a range at a time and totalled by its id while the list goes on changing. It lasts `minutes`, at most limits.snapshot_rows ids, and a list keeps at most limits.snapshots_kept (the oldest goes first).

file_moves._what: A file field names a file by its identity (1f:...) or by its name (/Media/clip.mp4). When a file moves or is renamed, rewriteFileNames (src/list-row-operations.mjs) puts the new name in every row of every list whose file field held the old one, each row only if it still holds it, a page at a time within limits.file_scan_rows, and says how many it rewrote and whether it reached the end. Names are compared exactly; an identity never needs rewriting.

duplicate._what: How a row is copied (src/list-row-operations.mjs duplicateRows), per field, as DATA: keep copies the value, drop leaves it out, reset puts back what a new row starts with (the field's `starts`, else nothing), remap keeps a link but points it at the copy when the row it names is copied too in the same request. A field names its own with `duplicate`; otherwise its kind row here decides; otherwise `default`. A field that settles on a value (Done) or starts on one is reset, so a copy of a finished row is open. What the row carries beside its fields (the basis of its values, where earlier rows were merged from) is never copied; the copy says where it came from (_copied_from).
duplicate._paired: A paired link (src/list-pairs.mjs) is left out of a copy unless the field says otherwise: keeping it would add the copy to the other side, which may hold only one row.

limit_notes._what: The two-stage limit (limits.warn_share): a write that uses this share of a limit still succeeds and answers `warnings` naming what is nearly full and what to do; one past the limit is refused by `too_many` with the same limit. A new limit that warns is one row here.

fields_per_list.remedy: Remove a field nothing reads, or keep the rest in a second list linked to this one.

lists_per_person.remedy: Remove a list you no longer use, or add a field to an existing list instead of making another.

views_per_list.remedy: Remove a view you no longer open.

rows_per_write.remedy: Send rows in groups below this size; a selection (select) changes any number of rows without naming them.

normalizers._what: How a kind's value is reduced to the form two spellings of the same thing share (a field kind row names one in `normalize`). Each is an ordered list of steps over the text: trim, lowercase, or replace (a JavaScript pattern, with the text it becomes). A row put with `match_on` finds the row already holding the same normalized value instead of making another; the raw spelling is always the one kept. A new normalizer is one row here.

domain_suffixes._what: Where a registrable domain starts (the domain_root normalizer, op registrable_root): a host ending in one of these two-label suffixes keeps three labels (shop.acme.co.uk -> acme.co.uk), any other keeps two (shop.acme.com -> acme.com). A host that is one label, or an address of numbers, is kept as it is. A new suffix is one entry here.

input_grammar._what: How text is read as a number or a date in a field that declares it (`input` on the field): decimal is the separator between the whole part and the fraction (the other mark, or a space, may group thousands), date_order is the order of day, month and year in a date written with / . or - between the parts (a date written year first is read as ISO whatever is declared). A field that declares nothing takes numbers as numbers and dates as the text it is given, as before.

source_namespaces._what: Row sources whose rows name their own values by namespace and key (src/list-paths.mjs sourceNamespacesOf): a saved view of a list with such a source may name note.status or file.mtime as it names a field, and the source says what kind each is (src/lists.mjs withRowSources sourceFields). Each row says which namespace holds what.

words.no_list: There is no list {list_id}. list_lists shows the lists this person keeps.
words.bad_id: A list or field id is a short name of letters, digits and dashes, like "trillion-crm"; {id} is not one.
words.bad_kind: The field {field_id} has the kind {kind}, which is not one of: {kinds}.
words.bad_link: The field {field_id} links to {links_to}, which is not a list this person keeps.
words.needs_link: The field {field_id} is a link, so it needs links_to: the id of the list it links to.
words.bad_value: The row {row_id} has a value for {field_id} that is not {expected}.
words.bad_link_constraints: The link rules for {field_id} are invalid. Acyclic links must point to rows in the same list.
words.link_too_many: The row {row_id} has too many links in {field_id}; keep at most {limit}.
words.link_target_missing: The row {row_id} links {field_id} to {target_id}, which is not a row this person keeps.
words.link_cycle: The link in {field_id} would make a cycle involving row {row_id}.
words.unknown_field: The row {row_id} has a value for {field_id}, which is not a field of {list_id}. save_list adds a field.
words.bad_balanced: The balanced rule for {list_id} needs amount_field (a number field), group_field (another field) and index (a declared index on just group_field), and cannot be used with managed rows.
words.balanced_index_building: The list {list_id} is still preparing the index its balanced rule needs. Try again shortly; nothing was written.
words.balanced_incomplete: The row {row_id} in {list_id} must have a number amount and an entry, because the list is balanced. An empty amount is not zero.
words.unbalanced_write: That write would leave the entry {group} in {list_id} adding to {sum}, not zero. Nothing was written. Put all of an entry's lines in one write.
words.bad_basis: The report basis {basis} is not one of: {bases}.
words.bad_opens_on: The list {list_id} opens on a saved view named by its id: give that id as text, or null for none.
words.bad_limit: The field {field_id} has a {key} that is not allowed: min and max are numbers on a number field, max_chars is a whole number on a text field, and min is not above max.
words.out_of_range: The row {row_id} has a value for {field_id} outside its limits (least {min}, most {max}, at most {max_chars} characters).
words.bad_row: Each row is { id?, values: { field_id: value } }; row {index} is not.
words.too_many: Keep at most {limit} {what} at a time.
words.too_long: The value for {field_id} in row {row_id} is longer than {limit} characters.
words.bad_view: Each saved view is { label, search?, rules? }, where rules is a filter rule group; view {index} is not.
words.bad_ref: A reference to a row is { address: "<list>/<row>" }, { list_id, row_id } or { list_id, key: { field_id, value } }, at most {limit} at a time; reference {index} is not.
words.bad_filter: A saved filter is { label, rules } where rules is a filter rule group { kind: "group", combinator, negate, rules }; {what}.
words.no_filter: The list {list_id} has no saved filter {filter_id}. Its filters are: {filters}.
words.filter_in_use: The saved filter {filter_id} is used by {users}; change or remove those first.
words.filter_cycle: The saved filter {filter_id} would use itself, through {through}.
words.no_view: The list {list_id} has no saved view {view_id}. Its views are: {views}.
words.page_links_too_large: This page has too many linked names to return at once. Request a smaller page.
words.needs_carried: The field {field_id} is a {kind} field, so it needs {key}: an object saying how its value is worked out (read_list field_kinds describes it).
words.needs_label: A list needs a label: the name people see, like "Trillion CRM".
words.bad_search: Search lists with q (the words), lists (list ids, comma separated), row_types (comma separated), holds (what the lists hold: {holds}) and limit; {what} is not allowed.
words.settled: The row {row_id} is {value} already, so {field_id} stays {value}: put a new row to ask again, or clear {field_id} with null to reopen it.
words.bad_order: This row cannot be moved in {list_id}. Choose a declared single-field text index and the row's current neighbours.
words.stale_order: The row order in {list_id} changed. Refresh the list and try the move again.
words.order_index_building: The row order in {list_id} is still being prepared. Try the move again after it finishes.
words.missing_required: The row {row_id} needs a value for {field_id}, which {list_id} requires. Give {field_id} a value.
words.required_cleared: {field_id} is required in {list_id}, so row {row_id} cannot clear it. Give it a new value instead.
words.ambiguous_number: The row {row_id} gives {field_id} the text {text}, and {field_id} does not say which mark is its decimal separator. Send a number, or set input: { decimal: "." } (or ",") on the field.
words.bad_number: The row {row_id} gives {field_id} the text {text}, which is not a number written with {decimal} as the decimal separator.
words.bad_date: The row {row_id} gives {field_id} the text {text}, which is not a real date written {order}, or year first.
words.bad_input: The field {field_id} declares input that is not { decimal: one of {decimals}, date_order: one of {orders} }.
words.bad_row_basis: The row {row_id} has a basis for {field_id} that is not { reasoning?: text, sources?: [texts, at most {sources}], confidence: high, medium or low }.
words.bad_match: match_on is a list of field ids of {list_id} whose kind has a normalizer or is plain text; {what} is not one.
words.match_ambiguous: The row with {field_id} {value} matches {count} rows of {list_id} ({ids}). Name the one with its id.
words.match_too_large: {list_id} holds more than {limit} rows, too many to match by {field_id} here. Name the row with its id.
words.bad_select: A selection is { view_id?: a saved view, or snapshot_id?: a snapshot's rows, except?: [row ids], include?: [row ids], cursor? }, with values to put in every selected row or remove: true; {what} is not allowed.
words.bad_aggregate: An aggregate is { view_id?, measures: [{ field?, op }] (1 to {measures}), group_by?: a field }, where op is one of: {ops}, and a measure other than count names a field of {kinds} kind it applies to; {what} is not allowed.
words.aggregate_unavailable: The formula engine is not available here, so the measures cannot be worked out.
words.merge_same: A row cannot be merged into itself.
words.bad_duplicate: A copy is { row_ids: [the rows to copy, at most {limit}], values?: what to put in every copy }; {what} is not allowed.
words.bad_duplicate_rule: The field {field_id} says duplicate: {rule}, which is not one of: {rules}.
words.merge_conflict: Both rows hold a value for {field_id} ({base} and {target}). Say which to keep with prefer: "base" or "target", or give the value in values.
words.bad_merge: A merge is { base_id: the row that goes, target_id: the row that stays, prefer?: "base" or "target", values? }; {what} is not allowed.
words.bad_path: The view {view_id} names the field {path}, which is not links followed by a field: every step before the last must be a link field, at most {hops} steps.
words.bad_preview: A preview takes the same rows and remove that put_list_rows takes, and writes nothing.
words.bad_pair: The field {field_id} pairs with {pairs_with} on {links_to}, which is not a link field there linking back to this list and naming {field_id} (or nothing) as its pair, in the same store.
words.bad_unique: The field {field_id} cannot be unique: only a text, email, phone, web address or tags field can be an identity key.
words.not_unique: {value} is held by row {holder} of {list_id} already, so row {row_id} cannot hold it in {field_id}, which is unique. Put the values in row {holder}, or merge the two rows.
words.unique_index_building: The identity keys of {list_id} are still being prepared, so a value cannot be checked as unique yet. Try again after they finish.
words.no_write_right: This write would change {list_id}, which you may not change. Ask its owner, or change only lists you may write.
words.bad_view_move: A view move is { view_id, anchor_id, placement: before or after } naming two different views of {list_id}: {views}.
words.bad_restore: A restore is { row_ids: [the removed rows to put back, at most {limit}] }.
words.bad_field_at: A read of a field at a moment is { field_id: a field of {list_id}, row_ids: [at most {limit} rows], at: an ISO time or a log row id }.
words.history_unavailable: The history of {list_id} is not kept where it lives, so it cannot be read as it was.
words.bad_snapshot: A snapshot holds at most {limit} rows; read the view with a narrower rule, or page it instead.
words.no_snapshot: There is no snapshot {snapshot_id} of {list_id}. read_list_snapshot needs the id a snapshot answered.
words.snapshot_expired: The snapshot {snapshot_id} lasted {minutes} minutes and is gone. Take a new one.
words.bad_match_mode: match_mode is one of {modes}; {what} is not one.
words.match_none: No row of {list_id} holds {value} in {field_id}, and match_mode {mode} makes no new row. Use create_or_update to make one.
words.match_exists: Row {row_id} of {list_id} holds {value} in {field_id} already, and match_mode {mode} only makes new rows. Use create_or_update to change it.
words.missing_parameter: The view {view_id} asks for the value {parameter} when it is read. Give it in parameters: { {parameter}: value }.
words.bad_relationship: The field {field_id} shows how well you know someone: { attribute: one of {attributes} }.
words.bad_review: A review action is one of {actions}: set_up takes expires_days (a number above 0), assign takes owner, the others take row_ids.
words.no_review: {list_id} is not set up for review; set it up first with review_list_rows action set_up.
words.needs_review: Changes to {list_id} by an AI wait for a person: propose them with propose_list_changes, and the person approves or declines them.
words.bad_proposal: A proposal names the rows it changes (rows with id and values, remove), each one of editable ({editable_most} at most), the scopes it looked in ({scopes_most} at most: { list_id, view_id? }) and its evidence ({evidence_most} at most: { list_id, row_id } within those scopes); {what} is not.
words.proposal_decided: Proposal {proposal_id} is {status}, so it cannot be {decision}; decisions are {decisions}.
words.person_decides: Only a person decides on proposal {proposal_id}; an AI proposes, and may withdraw what it proposed.
words.bad_history: The field {field_id} works its value out from a field's history: { field: a field of this list that says keeps_history: true, op: one of {ops}, value: for time_spent_in and has_been_in, at (an ISO time) or days_ago: for value_at, unit: one of {units} }.
words.bad_rollup: The field {field_id} works its value out from linked rows: { through?: a link field of this list (none: the row itself), field: a field of the list it links to, where?: a rule group, op: one of {ops} }; {what} is not.
words.bad_file_name: A file is named by where it is, a name starting with {prefix} (like /Media/clip.mp4); from and to are two different names.
words.bad_copy: A copy into another list is { row_ids: [at most {limit}], to_list, map?: { field of {to_list}: field of this list }, values? }; {what} is not allowed.
words.not_documents: The list {list_id} does not show a folder of documents; save it with row_sources [{ source: "{source}", of: <folder> }] first.
words.bad_document_types: A folder's property types are { types: { <property>: one of {kinds} }, formulas: { <name>: { binding: <formula>, kind? } } } with at most {formulas} formulas; {what} is not.
words.formula_cycle: The formula {formula} reads itself through {through}, so working it out would never end.
words.bad_document_property: A document's own properties are written as {properties}.<key> (a key of letters, digits, - and _); {what} cannot be written: file facts and formulas are worked out, and a document is removed as a file.
words.bad_property_value: The property {property} of {document} is a {kind}, and {value} is not one.
words.document_changed: The document {document} changed after it was read ({expected} is now {current}); read it again and make the change on what it says now.
words.not_a_document: {document} is not a text document in this folder.
words.bad_plain_files: A list's plain files are a folder with {what}.
